q: To access a secure facility, an engineer swipes a corporate badge and then scans an assigned RFID key fob against the sensor to unlock the door. Which statement accurately assesses this authentication process?
opts: The system enforced multifactor authentication by validating two independent electronic devices
The system performed contextual authentication by confirming the physical coordinates of the user
The system executed single-factor verification using two credentials from the same factor category
The system achieved mutual authentication by confirming trust across both communicating endpoints
exp: True MFA requires two or more *different* factor types (e.g., something you know, have, or are). Combining a badge and an RFID key fob merely pairs two possession factors, remaining single-factor authentication.

wrongFeedback.0: Presenting two separate physical items does not achieve multifactor authentication if both items belong to the same factor category ("something you have").
wrongFeedback.1: Contextual (adaptive) authentication evaluates environmental attributes—such as time of day, device posture, or IP geolocation—rather than possession tokens.
wrongFeedback.3: Mutual authentication requires both sides of a connection (client and server) to verify each other's identity, which is unrelated to a user presenting two credentials to an access reader.
